key_insight: Real-hardware quantum optimization is mostly noise-limited on today’s IBM Heron processors, with a practical fidelity threshold around F_est≈0.1 for MDKP/MIS and no viable QAP solutions found under the tested encodings.
engineering_relevance: Qubit-efficient formulations can enlarge runnable problem sizes, but circuit depth, two-qubit gate counts, and encoding feasibility remain the dominant constraints for deployable quantum optimization workflows.
method: Benchmarked VQE, CVaR-VQE, standard/multi-angle/warm-start QAOA, PCE, and QRAO on IBM Heron r1/r2.
Ran 247 method-instance combinations across MDKP, MIS, QAP, and MSP with resilience-level-2 mitigation.
Compared hardware outputs against an independent gate-count fidelity proxy (F_est) and a uniform-random control.
evidence_signal: Across 247 runs, compiled QAOA-family circuits were generally noise dominated; QAP’s one-hot feasible space was extremely sparse (10!/2^100 at n=10), and the SWAP-aware counterfactual still stayed below F_est=10^-3.
watch_item: Results are specific to the tested implementations, encodings, and hardware/compiler settings, so they should not be generalized to QAOA or quantum optimization broadly.
paper_title: From Circuits to Hardware: Benchmarking Standard and Qubit-Efficient Quantum Optimization on Real Hardware
